bib.title: Appendix A: Introduction to graphs (Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action)
bib.venue: book appendix; excerpted from Alessandro's previous book [1]

question: What are the basic concepts of graphs, how do graphs model networks, and how are graphs represented for processing?

results.claim: A graph is G = (V, E), a set of vertices and edges; edges may be directed or undirected, weighted or unweighted.
Adjacency list memory is proportional to |V| + |E|; the lists sum to |E| entries for a directed graph and 2 x |E| for an undirected one.
results.setup: Any graph G = (V, E) stored as adjacency lists
results.quote: If G is an undirected graph, the sum of the lengths of all the adjacency lists is 2 × |E|.

results.claim: An adjacency matrix needs memory proportional to |V| x |V| regardless of edge count, with one bit per entry for unweighted graphs; undirected matrices are symmetric so half can be stored.
results.quote: The adjacency matrix of a graph requires memory directly proportional to |V| × |V|, independent of the number of edges in the graph.

results.claim: Adjacency lists suit sparse graphs; matrices suit dense graphs or when fast edge-existence checks are needed. Lists give no faster edge test than searching Adj[u].
results.note: The text defines sparse as 'number of edges is less than the number of vertices', which is stricter than the usual definition.

results.claim: In the 2008 Amazon also-bought network of US political books, red and blue clusters had no connections or intermediaries; by 2012 many books bridged the clusters.
results.setup: Amazon top political books, US, 2008 vs 2012; books linked if often bought by the same customer

results.claim: Homophily: links in social networks tend to connect similar people; this helps recommend to new users with no history via connected users.
The Panama Papers analysis extracted entities and relationships from leaked documents into a network, revealing offshore structures that traditional data mining could not.
results.setup: Leaked financial documents; visual graph tools
results.note: Text dates the Panama Papers to 2023; the text does not give another year.

limits: Introductory, no experiments; excerpted from the author's earlier book.
Says nothing about property graphs, RDF, Cypher or knowledge graphs; only basic graph theory and storage representations.
Figure references in the degree paragraphs look inconsistent: the directed-graph degree example cites figure A.5 though the directed graph is A.3; the undirected degree example cites A.4.
practices: Use an adjacency list for sparse graphs (A.3).
Use an adjacency matrix for small or dense graphs, or when quick edge-existence tests are needed (A.3).
When storing directed graphs, choose one direction (outgoing or ingoing) and keep it consistent (A.3).
Keep vertex numbering consistent over the life of an adjacency matrix (A.3).
Consider surrounding contexts (e.g. homophily) when modelling networks, since they drive how structure evolves (A.2).

terms.definition: a data structure consisting of a set of vertices (or nodes/points) and edges (or relationships/lines) that can be used to model relationships among a collection of objects
a graph in which we assign names and meanings to the edges and vertices
the total number of edges incident to that vertex, which is also equal to the number of neighbors of that vertex
number of edges for which the vertex is the end node (head) / start node (tail)
a sequence of vertices with consecutive pairs connected by an edge; a path with no repeating vertices; a path in which the first and last vertex coincide
all the vertices of G are pairwise adjacent
edges carry a numerical value used to convey some significance
links in a social network tend to connect people who are similar to one another
factors that exist outside the vertices and edges of a network but that nonetheless affect how the network's structure evolves
an array Adj of lists, one per vertex, where Adj[u] holds all vertices adjacent to u
a |V| x |V| matrix A = (a_uv) with a_uv = 1 if the edge exists, else 0 (the weight for weighted graphs)
